prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · REST endpoints (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Endpoint" · longest unbreakable word 261px · one-line width 261px
  col 2: header "Method" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Auth" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 4: header "Rate limit" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 85px · one-line width 670px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A compact REST API reference table: readers find an endpoint, then check its method, auth requirement, rate limit, and description.","reading":"Rows are read endpoint-first; the path is the row key, Method/Auth/Rate limit are quick qualifiers scanned across rows, and Description is read last as prose.","groups":["Method, Auth, Rate limit: compact request constraints that belong together and are compared across rows","Endpoint: standalone row identifier and primary scan target","Description: free prose, secondary to route identification"],"keep_intact":["full endpoint path and path parameters such as {jobId}","HTTP methods GET, POST, DELETE","auth values Bearer and Admin","rate-limit tokens such as 600/min"],"may_wrap":["Description text","header labels such as Rate limit and Description","endpoint path only as a deliberate last resort when avoiding horizontal scroll"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [282, 76, 67, 89, 221] · table 736×415px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 60, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 376px
Design r1B: widths [282, 76, 67, 89, 151] · table 666×578px · row heights [36, 153, 153, 83, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 306px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r1A","good":"Endpoint and Method both survive intact and on one line, headers never wrap, no mid-word splits, and Method/Auth/Rate limit sit shoulder-to-shoulder as a compact constraint block right after the row key. The endpoint path, which is the row's identity, is never mangled.","problems":"The box shows only Endpoint and Method (plus a clipped sliver of Auth); Rate limit and Description — the two columns a reader most needs after the route — are entirely off-screen. Worse, every row is 106px tall while the Endpoint cell holds a single 20px line: ~70px of dead white space under each path, repeated 4 times. The table reads as an empty grid with text pushed to the left edge.","cause":"Description got 221px (200px of text) so its prose wraps to 4 lines; those 4 lines set the row height for the whole row. Meanwhile the four left columns consume 282+76+67+89 = 514px before Description begins, so the table is 736px wide yet still starves the only column that needs width."},{"design":"r1B","good":"Same strengths as r1A — intact endpoint, unwrapped headers, no word splits — and it is 70px narrower, so slightly less horizontal scroll.","problems":"Everything r1A does wrong, worse. Description at 151px becomes a 6-line ribbon of 3–4 words per line; rows balloon to 153px and the table to 578px tall. The endpoint column now has ~130px of blank space per row, so the visual weight of the table is white space rather than data. The reader scrolls right to find a description that is unreadable in a 130px measure anyway.","cause":"Trading 70px of table width away from Description cost 2 extra lines per row × 5 rows ≈ +160px of height. Description is the wrong column to squeeze: it is the only one with 670px of one-line content, so it is the only one whose width change moves row height at all."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"tight-2line","widths":[282,76,67,89,370],"change":"Keeps Endpoint intact (282), the constraint trio at their natural minima (76/67/89), and gives Description the smallest width that still yields 2 lines (370 = 349px text ≈ 2×335). Total 884px instead of 736–666, i.e. more scroll, but row heights drop from 106/153px to roughly 60px and the table becomes ~330px tall — the white space under the endpoint disappears, and Description becomes scannable prose instead of a 3-word ribbon. This is the best height-per-pixel-of-scroll trade in the set."},{"name":"compact-3line","widths":[282,76,67,89,244],"change":"A deliberate lean toward less scrolling: Description at 244px (223px text) gives 3 lines, so rows are ~80px and the table ~410px tall, at a total of 758px — only 22px wider than r1A but with two fewer description lines per row. Use this if the reader's workflow is 'scroll rarely, read the description fully once'."},{"name":"flat-wide","widths":[282,76,67,89,691],"change":"The unexplored alternative: give Description its full one-line width (691) so every row is a single 36px line and the whole table is ~250px tall — a true spreadsheet-like reference. Total 1205px means heavy horizontal scrolling, but row rhythm is perfect, comparison across rows is trivial, and no cell is ever a ragged column of short lines. Worth it if the table is used for scanning/verifying rather than reading prose in place."}]}
